name: LinkedIn
use_case: sign users in and post on their behalf (member posting); optionally manage company pages

verdict.label: Easy · same day
verdict.summary: Posting as the member is self-serve the same day. But tokens last 60 days with no refresh token unless you're an approved partner, so users must reconnect every two months. Anything involving company Pages or analytics is a separate, vetted, partner-style application with no guaranteed approval.
verdict.wait: None for member posting; Community Management API approval: no published time
verdict.gating_step: Company-page access (Community Management API) is vetted; member tokens expire every 60 days without partner refresh tokens

concept: A LinkedIn developer app is created in the Developer Portal and must be associated with a LinkedIn Page. API access comes from the products you add to the app. Some are self-serve (Sign In with LinkedIn, Share on LinkedIn); others require an access request and vetting. Each member who connects grants the app a token limited to the products' scopes.

paths.name: Sign in + post as the member
paths.when: Your agent drafts and publishes posts on the user's own profile. Self-serve products: Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect plus Share on LinkedIn (w_member_social).

paths.name: Manage company Pages (Community Management API)
paths.when: Posting as an organization, reading page analytics or comments. Requires an access request, vetting, a verified Page, and a dedicated app.

composio.managed_note: Composio's LinkedIn toolkit lists a Composio-managed OAuth app (OAuth2).
when_own_app: Production: users should see your app name on the consent screen, not “Composio”.
You need scopes beyond Composio's defaults.
You need your own rate-limit quota (managed apps share quota across Composio users).
You need faster polling triggers than the managed 15-minute minimum.
Self-hosted or regional instances of the provider.

stages.name: Build & test (works today)
stages.summary: Member sign-in and posting are self-serve products you add in the portal.

limits.text: Share on LinkedIn: 150 requests per member per day and 100,000 per application per day (UTC).
Access tokens are valid for 60 days by default. Programmatic refresh tokens are only for approved Marketing Developer Platform partners.

steps.title: Have (or create) a LinkedIn Page for your company
steps.detail: Apps must be associated with a Page. If you're its admin, verifying the app against it is quick.

steps.title: Create the app in the Developer Portal
steps.detail: linkedin.com/developers/apps → Create app → associate the Page, logo and privacy policy URL.

steps.title: Verify the app with the Page admin
steps.detail: Send the verification link to a Page admin, or approve it yourself if you are one.

steps.title: Add products: Sign In with LinkedIn (OIDC) + Share on LinkedIn
steps.detail: Products tab. This grants openid, profile, email and w_member_social.

steps.title: Add the redirect URL and create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Auth tab → Authorized redirect URLs → Composio's callback URL. Then copy the Client ID and secret into Composio.

steps.title: Connect and post a test
steps.detail: Use a private or test profile. Posts are real.

stages.name: Go to production
stages.summary: Member posting needs no review. Company-page features are a separate application process.

steps.title: Plan for 60-day re-consent
steps.detail: Without partner refresh tokens, prompt users to reconnect before day 60, and handle revoked tokens by falling back to the login flow.

steps.title: For company Pages: create a dedicated app
steps.detail: The Community Management API must be the only product on its app; the request button is greyed out if other products are attached.

steps.title: Request Community Management API (Development tier)
steps.detail: Complete the access form. LinkedIn vets both the developer and the app against its terms and supported use cases. Legal name, address, website and privacy policy should all line up.

steps.title: Upgrade to Standard tier
steps.detail: Submit the Standard-tier form, a screen recording of your app, and test credentials.

requirements.item: LinkedIn Page associated with the app

requirements.detail: Required for Community Management API vetting.
For the Community Management Standard tier.

gotchas.title: Users must reconnect every ~60 days
gotchas.detail: Long-running agents silently lose LinkedIn access unless you're an approved partner with refresh tokens. Build reminders.

gotchas.title: Company-page features need a separate app
gotchas.detail: The Community Management API can't share an app with other products, so plan two apps and two auth configs.

gotchas.title: Approval is discretionary
gotchas.detail: Rejections often come down to how the use case is described, not your code.

gotchas.title: Token TTL units in LinkedIn's docs are inconsistent
gotchas.detail: The sample responses' expires_in values don't match the stated 60 and 365 days in seconds. Read the real response before writing expiry logic.

blockers.symptom: Community Management “Request access” is greyed out
blockers.cause: The app already has other products or pending requests.
blockers.fix: Create a new app on the same Page just for Community Management.

blockers.symptom: “Identity vetting failed” / access denied for org endpoints
blockers.cause: The app isn't approved for the Community Management API, or business verification failed.
blockers.fix: Complete the access request with consistent company details.
Ask the user to reconnect; schedule reminders before expiry.

agent: Decide which products your use case actually needs
you: Own or admin a LinkedIn Page and verify the app
Create the app(s) and add products
Submit access forms as the business

uncertainties: Community Management review timelines aren't published.
Whether a Page is strictly required for self-serve-only apps is stated by third-party guides; LinkedIn's own pages we read only state it for Community Management.
